where: crates/hir-ty-pure/src/walk.rs `summary_in`, through crates/hir-ty-mir/src/mir/dispatch.rs `body_of` (the `monomorphized_runtime_mir_body*` queries, `lru = 0, mem_tag = Mir`)
what: A cold build of tempo (eb3376ba8c, blaze d45e70ddc) ran its last unit's codegen alone on one worker for over 5 minutes while the footprint rose from 89.8 to 121.8 GiB; the daemon's release then let go of 4,197,786 MIR bodies. Lane reth's allocation stacks put the top site, `monomorphized`, under `hir_ty_pure::walk::summary_in` recursing: the purity summary that `SpendFacts` asks of each direct callee walks the callee's whole closure depth first on one query stack and read every instance's body from a memo that keeps it until the build ends.
cost: tempo's cold build did not finish (stopped at 2,073 s); the lane first guessed coroutine layout and promoted constants from the code and reported that before the stacks arrived
whys: Why was the memory held? One monomorphized body per instance stayed in a query memo on the global heap.
Why a memo? `dispatch::body_of` was the only way to get an instance's body, and it is the interpreter's entry, which needs the memo because it runs one body many times.

Why did a walk that reads each body once use the interpreter's entry? Nothing distinguishes a value read once from one read often: every query result is kept by default, and `lru = 0` means kept until someone asks.
Why did nothing notice? The memo's count is by tag, not by query and not by instances per body, and the walk's span said nothing while it ran.
Why one worker? A summary asks its callees' summaries inside its own run, so the closure is one stack of queries; the pool only sees one job.
cause: a per-instance value with a per-item lifetime kept in a per-build memo, read by a walk whose result is the only thing that outlives the item
class: per-instance memo of a derived body: memory that grows with instances reached, not with code written (the same class: `monomorphized_promoted_mir_body_query`, `db.monomorphized_mir` in layout.rs:676 and debuginfo/types.rs:644, `body_of` in hir-ty-identity walk.rs and hir-ty-suspend summary.rs)
prevention: written: `dispatch::body_once` (owned, dropped by the caller) and `summary_in` on it, with hir-ty-pure tests::held (MIR values held are equal for 8 and 64 instances of one generic; the control reads the memo). To build: a gate check that lists every `lru = 0` query whose key holds generic arguments (`StoredGenericArgs`) and whose value is a `MirBody`, and fails on one not on a short list with its reason (the interpreter's); and a per-query count of held values in `blaze explain memory`, so instances per body is a number someone can read
